lead: Rheinmetall / RHM — Germany rearms and the dip is the buy
smaller: Bitcoin / BTC — the government just became a holder
Sandisk / SNDK — the relisted stock with nearly 70% upside
Tesla / TSLA — the boycott is now a bargain
why_lead: Repeat of the 5 March lead, kept because today's evidence changed. Reuters (6 March) reported that retail traders were behind Eutelsat's 650% surge and called it the GameStop effect; Eutelsat then slipped on Ukraine prospects (7 March); the WSJ (8 March) described European defence stocks as a hedge-fund home run; and the card shows Rheinmetall up 54.13% over 20 sessions but down 7.01% in the latest session, a sharp drawdown the crowd is buying. The hook is new (the dip), and no other trade in the feed pairs a card move, retail attention and a simple crowd story as directly. Hook shortened to eight words; Citi note corrected to say it covers US defence names; euro-listed wording fixed.
why_smaller: Bitcoin: changed story. The 6 March smaller awaited the reserve reveal. The executive order was signed on 6 March, after that edition's cutoff, and bitcoin still fell (CNBC, 6 March). The card shows bitcoin down 15.84% over 20 sessions.

Sandisk: no earlier appearance. Western Digital's exit from SSDs and SanDisk's takeover of the flash business (6 and 7 March), plus a Stocktwits item of 4 March on an analyst's near-70% upside with retail excited. The card has no 20-session figure (sixteen observations), so the trade uses only the one-session and five-session moves.

Tesla: fifth appearance, so the 4 March bull case (Morgan Stanley top pick, Cathie Wood) and the 5 and 6 March sales and India angles were dropped as already used. The story changed on 7 to 9 March: used-car prices crashed (Forbes, 9 March), Fortune says Tesla is flailing in China as BYD rises (9 March), and showroom protests reached Portugal and Australia (Reuters and ABC, 9 March).
considered_not_chosen: Rigetti / RGTI (quantum): the 7 March lead already used the same Quantum Day catalyst and 'revolution' hook. The only new item is CNBC's 'meme stock' remark (7 March). Dropped to avoid a three-day repeat.

Robinhood / HOOD: Reddit trending list (7 March), trivia players (6 March) and a $29.75 million regulator settlement (7 March). Not chosen because its crypto-contest angle overlaps the bitcoin smaller; kept as a candidate for a later edition.
Hims & Hers / HIMS: a failed narrative (down 20.27% over five sessions; Apostrophe shutdown and a judge's compounding ruling on 7 March), but the feed has no Stocktwits or Reddit item for it.
Nebius / NBIS: a 7 March smaller on the same 5 March data-centre news.
Alibaba / BABA: the 6 March lead; the China AI rally has no new retail-attention item.
Palantir / PLTR: a 6 March smaller on the DOGE angle. The Karp share-sale headline (6 March) is the only new catalyst, with no retail-attention item.
Dogecoin / DOGE-USD: a 7 March smaller ('meme coin dream fading'); the further 35% fall is the same angle.
Nuclear and AI power (OKLO, VST, CEG): large drawdowns, but the feed's nuclear items are policy and deal news, and NuScale was a smaller on 4 March.
Eutelsat: the GameStop-effect story supports the lead, but Eutelsat is not on the market card, so it cannot carry a trade on its own price.
Intuitive Machines, Wolfspeed and other Stocktwits names: not on the market card, so they cannot be priced from it.
